conviction_note: XYF has traded off the controlling holder's US$6.03/ADS take-private proposal since 2026-11-06. The controlling holder has about 94% of the votes and needs no minority approval, so the Q3 numbers have little path to the price. The stock sits 12.9% below the offer and has drifted down since the pop. The bar is unsourced (no consensus found), so every finding is capped small. The findings sum to -0.5: a weak peer print and the regulatory squeeze lean negative, while the deal floor, the wide spread and the 0.17x book lean positive. The scaled number is (2*0.47-1)*3.5 = -0.21, near zero, because the deal pin dominates the quarter and the lean rests on proxies.

next_guide.company_current_guide: none. The CFO on the Q2 call (2026-08-24): 'we are not providing quantitative guidance for the third quarter at this time'. Management will 'resume providing guidance when visibility improves'. https://www.webull.com/news/15460662063678464
next_guide.basis: No guide has been given since the regulatory reset. The company is now under a take-private proposal, which discourages forward commentary. The closest peer (Qfin, 2026-11-24) guided Q4 net income down 67-77% YoY and spoke of 'clear erosion in risk performance', so any qualitative outlook XYF gives is more likely cautious than constructive.

findings.finding: Peer Qfin Holdings (ex-Qifu) reported Q3 2026 on 2026-11-24 after the close. Loan volume was RMB49.5bn (-40.6% YoY), net income RMB380.5m (low end of its own RMB360-460m Q3 guide), and the CEO cited 'clear erosion in risk performance' on a 'significantly downsized loan book in the third quarter and into recent months'. Q4 net income was guided to RMB210-310m (-67% to -77% YoY). QFIN fell 7.6% on 2026-11-25 (4.61 to 4.26) on about 4x its normal volume. XYF's Q2 trend was the opposite: delinquency improving QoQ, and management saying contraction had 'moderated meaningfully'. That read predates this peer data, which points to further volume decline and credit deterioration across the sector in Q3. No XYF consensus exists to compare against.
findings.link: Same business: both facilitate unsecured consumer loans in China funded by bank partners. Both operate under the same NFRA internet-lending notice (effective 2025-10-01) and the 24% all-in APR cap, and draw on the same pool of bank funding partners. XYF is smaller and has weaker credit (91-180 day DPD 9.09% at Q2 against QFIN's 90+ day 2.50%). No shared-customer figure.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Before the proposal, XYF sold off on weak results: Q3 2025 -15.7% and Q4 2025 -26.19%; Q1 2026 -2.87% and Q2 2026 +2.04% (baseline history; dates match the results 6-Ks). On 2026-11-25, while pinned by the bid, XYF ignored QFIN's print (+0.4%, 5.23 to 5.25).
findings.why_not_priced: XYF did not move when QFIN fell 7.6% on 2026-11-25. Its price is set by the US$6.03 proposal, not by the sector, so the sector's Q3 deterioration has not been marked into XYF. If it had, XYF would have fallen with QFIN and FINV (-20.7% and -15.6% since 11-10, against XYF -1.7%). The pin is also why the effect is small: a weak quarter matters only if it makes the buyer lower its price.
findings.independence: Same direction: the industry article of 2026-10-16 quotes LexinFintech expecting a sharp QoQ fall in Q3 loan issuance and a possible net loss, and an analyst expecting weaker players to be dropped from funding lists (https://www.itiger.com/news/1166738260). QFIN price data: https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/QFIN?range=1mo&interval=1d

findings.finding: Since the proposal day XYF has fallen from 5.75 to 5.25 (-8.7%), so it trades 12.9% below the US$6.03/ADS offer (the offer is 14.9% above spot). The spread already prices meaningful doubt about whether the deal completes. A release that carries any deal-progress language (special committee advisers named, negotiations under way) or confirms the buyer's intent would tighten the spread. A release that simply omits the deal leaves the stock where it is.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The only deal-related events so far: proposal 2026-11-06 +22.34%; special committee 6-K 2026-11-19 -0.19%, with the stock drifting lower afterwards (5.27 to 5.18 to 5.25).
findings.why_not_priced: The width of the spread is the market's price of deal risk. What is not priced is any progress the release discloses. If the market expected progress, the spread would have narrowed towards 6.03 since the committee formed on 11-18, not widened.
findings.independence: Offer terms: 13D exhibit 99.2 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1725033/000110465926123916/tm2629217d1_ex99-2.htm). Shares the proposal documents with the next finding.

findings.finding: A 6-K of 2026-11-19 shows the board formed a special committee of three independent directors (Zheng Wan, Zheng Xue, Longgen Zhang) on 2026-11-18. It names no advisers and gives no timetable; the company does not commit to updates. The 13D of 2026-11-06 shows Mangrove Coast and Yue Tang hold 47.97% of shares and about 94% of votes. Financing is to be third-party debt plus equity 'in the form of cash and/or rollover equity'. The proposal letter names no majority-of-minority condition, so the controlling holder can carry the vote alone. The Q3 numbers therefore have little path to the outcome, and the bid works as a floor.
findings.why_not_priced: Both documents are public, and the deal-control structure is in the price as the reason XYF ignored its peers. What is not priced is the Q3 release possibly adding to it, for example naming committee advisers or reiterating the timeline.
findings.independence: 13D primary document with ownership and Item 3 funding: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1725033/000110465926123916/xslSCHEDULE_13D_X02/primary_doc.xml. Shares the proposal with the finding above.

findings.finding: At 2026-06-30, total equity was RMB7,755.4m (US$1,143.0m) on 221.6m ordinary shares (about 36.9m ADS-equivalents at 6 shares per ADS), which is about US$31 of book per ADS. The US$6.03 offer is 0.19x book and spot is 0.17x. Cash and equivalents were US$166.8m (about US$4.5/ADS) plus RMB827.7m restricted cash. The Q3 release will restate book and cash; a large cash balance against a low offer gives minority holders and the committee grounds to push for a higher price.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No history of the stock reacting to book value. It traded at deep discounts to book through 2025-26.
findings.why_not_priced: The book is public, and Chinese lenders have traded at deep discounts to book for years, so this is mostly priced. The only unpriced part is a Q3 cash or book figure that sharpens the offer-versus-book gap while a committee is negotiating. If the market expected a bump, XYF would trade at or above 6.03, not 13% below.

findings.finding: The US$100m buyback runs only until 2026-11-30. About US$35.5m remained as of 2026-08-14, and management said it was 'doing almost the maximum buyback in the normal buybacks'. Buybacks are very likely frozen while a take-private is pending, and the Q3 release may confirm the programme lapses unrenewed. The semi-annual dividend comes with the Q2 and Q4 results, so none is due with Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not separable. Buybacks ran through 2026 while the stock fell from about 7.4 to 4.7.
findings.why_not_priced: The expiry date is public, but nobody has said whether the programme is renewed. Losing a buyer that bought near the maximum in a stock trading about US$0.5m a day matters for a thin tape. If the market expected renewal, the stock would not have drifted from 5.75 to 5.25 without a bid.
findings.independence: The buyback figures and expiry are also in the Q2 release (https://finviz.com/news/384651/x-financial-reports-second-quarter-2026-unaudited-financial-results).

findings.finding: The regulatory squeeze is still running. China Daily (2026-10-22) reports banks cutting platform partnerships by more than 80%, e.g. Jilin Yillion Bank from 56 partners to 10, with small platforms expected to exit or be acquired. In the Q2 call (2026-08-24) XYF disclosed that business with one funding institution 'is already basically gone', that the institution had not returned XYF's guarantee deposit, and booked a RMB95.3m provision on deposits and other financial assets. Q3 carries the risk of further deposit write-downs or lost funding partners.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 print that carried the RMB95.3m deposit provision was met with +2.04%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a sector-to-company link, and XYF has not quantified any Q3 exposure. If priced, the offer spread would reflect a lower-price risk; instead the stock is pinned and has not reacted to sector news.
findings.independence: The company's own disclosure of the lost funding partner and RMB95.3m provision: https://www.webull.com/news/15460662063678464. The industry article quoting an analyst on weaker players being dropped from funding lists: https://www.itiger.com/news/1166738260

baseline_tension: There is no options market and no skew. The 20d run-up of +8.25% is the proposal pop, and since then the stock has given back 8.7% while the offer spread widened. My slight negative lean (peer credit erosion, regulatory squeeze) agrees with that drift. It is offset by the bid floor, which the controlling holder can carry alone, so p_up stays near 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar unsourced): confirmed the cap; every finding was already at or under 0.8 points, so nothing else changed.
Rule 5 / rule 1 (proxy, verified fact is not a reaction): the QFIN peer finding was cut from -0.8 to -0.7. It is a sector proxy for a name whose price is pinned by the bid.
Rebuilt the reaction base rate from confirmed results 6-Ks (Q3'25 -15.7, Q4'25 -26.19, Q1'26 -2.87, Q2'26 +2.04), as the file asks where baseline_history_trustworthy is false; finding kept at -0.3.

Rule 8 (understatement): abs_move_pct raised from 3.0 to 3.5. The bid caps the upside at about +15% and pre-bid support sits about 10% lower, so the move is bounded but the thin tape and half-day session can still move it.
'Asking what the market missed generates pessimism': p_up moved from 45 to 47, because the negative lean rests on proxies against a bid floor.
Rule 7 (positioning): short interest is low and falling (DTC 1.0), so the negatives were not shrunk for squeeze risk.
